title: Compute brief - 2 November 2026
description: Credit, not chips, is the new constraint: CoreWeave, Nebius and Nscale are effectively shut out of the bond market, and Nvidia is negotiating to guarantee debt for Nscale's Anthropic campus in West Virginia. Korea arranges its first GPU loan, about 10.7 trillion won for Brookfield and Naver. Marvell buys Lumentum at a $115 billion enterprise value to own the optical link. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: The AI build-out now runs on credit
lede: After a week of record hyperscaler backlogs, the weekend story was who pays for the buildings. The Wall Street Journal reported that CoreWeave, Nebius and Nscale have effectively been shut out of the high-yield bond market, with CoreWeave's 9.75% notes now trading above a 15% yield, Lambda cutting its target valuation from $14.5 billion to $13 billion, and Nscale's IPO leaning toward December. Where bonds will not go, vendors and banks are stepping in: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions of debt for the first 460 MW building of Nscale's West Virginia campus, which Anthropic has contracted for about $44.6 billion, and KB Kookmin Bank will arrange about 10.7 trillion won of loans secured on Naver Cloud's long-term GPU contract, Korea's first GPU financing. In hardware, Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion to combine electrical and optical interconnect. On the public tape all 70 list prints confirmed; Lambda H100 holds at $3.99 and B200 at $6.69 per GPU-hour.
